answer.thought: The headline on the Calcutta court case is a curious inversion of my logic. The court acts to preserve the universal, yet the means are criminal contempt, a private punishment for a public wrong. The vaccine statistics show the state reaching into the body of the citizen, but the gap between Kerala and Mumbai reminds me that the universal is not yet actual in every particular. I will make a note of the contempt proceedings; it is a struggle between the individual and the state that has no ethical resolution in the current configuration.
